quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: Only if you are in a crash.
If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. You must show proof of insurance and your license to an officer when asked during a traffic stop or after a crash.

questions.question: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind motorcycles. They can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes suddenly. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one taillight.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if a traffic light is not working?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
If the intersection looks clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop. Look both ways and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.

questions.question: If your vehicle skids on water, you should quickly apply the brakes.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not use the brakes right away. Try to regain control. If you cannot, release the gas pedal and let the skid stop on its own.

questions.question: How do you yield to an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop right away, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop inside an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: When you see an accident scene ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if you were involved or if emergency help has not arrived.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Keep your focus on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not stop just to look at the accident.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: You are in the left lane of two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. The driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic can flow.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass other vehicles, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than traffic around you, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" happens when:

options.text: You stare at the road for long periods of time.
You sleep too much the night before.
You drive short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stare at the road for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead at the road for too long and stop checking your mirrors and surroundings. You can zone out and miss traffic slowing or stopping ahead of you, which can cause a crash.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop immediately and back up.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They warn that work is happening on or next to the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: What is the best way to keep yourself and others safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before you shift into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio before backing up to alert people nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is risky because drivers cannot see well behind their vehicles. Walk to the back and check for children and small objects before you start backing up.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects.
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and reduces its effects.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Where should your car be positioned to make a right turn?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road before turning right. Do not cut across lanes of traffic.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Staying focused on the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let oncoming traffic go first. You can only turn when it is safe and oncoming traffic is not affected.

questions.question: To avoid losing control on wet roads, increase your vehicle's speed.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your tires can slide on water (hydroplaning), causing you to lose control. Slow down when driving in wet conditions to avoid hydroplaning.

questions.question: You do not need to keep as much distance behind a motorcycle as behind a car.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions. Keep 3 to 4 seconds of distance behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to react in an emergency.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing the intersection.
Always come to a full stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign tells you to slow down and let other traffic and pedestrians go first. Be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left can then go when it is safe.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity relate to vehicle speed?

options.text: They are not affected by speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers have time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, which direction should you look first?

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left, then right, then left again before entering an intersection. Vehicles from your left are closer than those from your right, so check your left side twice. Also look across the whole intersection to make sure it is clear.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire suddenly blows out while driving?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and leave the traffic lane.
Pump the brakes several times quickly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and leave the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, stay calm. Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the accelerator. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Lightly apply the brakes only when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed enough.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, what must a driver do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and yield to them, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?

options.text: Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and take another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and take another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Even shallow water can hide dangers. Turn around and find a different way to get where you are going.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They prepare you for upcoming hazards. This sign tells you that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready to stop for a red light or respond to other traffic signals.

questions.question: Which one of these must you obey over the others?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over all signs, signals, and road markings. Other authorized traffic directors include fire police, highway work zone flag persons, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go in the direction the green arrow points if you are in the right lane, regardless of other signals. Always yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection before turning.

questions.question: White lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. Solid white lines mark the edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate lanes going opposite directions.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross, even without a marked crosswalk. Pedestrians have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Look carefully for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: When changing lanes, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, use your turn signal, and look for other vehicles. Do not use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap, match the traffic speed, signal, and then:

options.text: Expect traffic to make room for you since you have the right-of-way.
Wait for the lane to completely clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap, speed up to match traffic, and signal. Merge safely when the gap is open. Stay alert and do not expect other drivers to move for you.
